$comment: Shared golden vectors for cycle prediction. Single source of truth consumed by BOTH the TypeScript reference test (src/services/cycle-prediction-reference.test.ts) and, by design, ovumcy-web's Go reference test (internal/services/cycles_reference_test.go). The two prediction implementations — cycle-prediction-policy.ts and cycles.go — are hand-parallel ports; these vectors enforce parity so a change to either that diverges from the other fails CI. Any prediction-math change MUST update this file, docs/cycle-prediction.md, and both reference tests in the same change. Dates are calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD), timezone-independent. See docs/cycle-prediction.md for the derivation of each case.

vectors.name: 15-day cycle, luteal 14 clamped to 10, window clamped to period start (non-exact)
14-day cycle -> below the 15-day floor, no prediction
25-day cycle, personalised luteal 11 across the end of February (exact)
vectors.$comment: Hand-derived by calendar arithmetic, not by running the code. Step 1: 11 >= 10, kept as 11. Step 2: 25 >= 15; reserve 25-5 = 20 >= 11, no clamp, so exact; ovulation day = 25-11 = 14 (>= 5). Ovulation date = 2026-02-20 + 13 days: February 2026 has 28 days, so Feb 20 + 8 = Feb 28, + 5 = 2026-03-05. Step 3: window start = Mar 5 - 5 days = 2026-02-28 (after the period start, no clamp); window end = 2026-03-05. Step 4: next period = 2026-02-20 + 25 days = Feb 28 + 17 = 2026-03-17. Check: Mar 5 -> Mar 17 is 12 calendar days, i.e. the ovulation day plus 11 following luteal days.

vectors.name: 32-day cycle, personalised luteal 16 (exact)
vectors.$comment: Hand-derived by calendar arithmetic, not by running the code. Step 1: 16 >= 10, kept as 16. Step 2: 32 >= 15; reserve 32-5 = 27 >= 16, no clamp, so exact; ovulation day = 32-16 = 16. Ovulation date = 2026-07-15 + 15 days = 2026-07-30. Step 3: window start = Jul 30 - 5 days = 2026-07-25; window end = 2026-07-30. Step 4: next period = 2026-07-15 + 32 days: July has 31 days, so Jul 15 + 16 = Jul 31, + 16 = 2026-08-16. Check: Jul 30 -> Aug 16 is 17 calendar days, i.e. the ovulation day plus 16 following luteal days.

projection.$comment: ADDITIVE section (lands in ovumcy-app via its twin PR). Pins the projection/anchor layer that production layers ON TOP of the base window math in `vectors`. Given a cycle-length history plus `lastPeriodStart`, `today`, and an IANA `timezone`, it locks: (1) the median-first prediction length (predictedCycleLength in cycles.go / cycle-prediction-policy.ts), (2) the projected current-cycle start and 1-based cycle day (ProjectCycleStart), (3) the displayed next-period date, which closes the RUNNING cycle (`lastPeriodStart` + prediction length, never rolled a cycle forward: on cycle day m+1 the period is due now, not a cycle later), and (4) the ovulation date after the single forward roll (ShiftCycleStartToFutureOvulation) that keeps ovulation on/after `today`. All arithmetic is calendar-day based and DST-immune, so the Europe/Berlin 2026-03-29 spring-forward case must project identically to a UTC run. Histories stay within the recent-cycle window (<= 6) so no tail truncation applies. Consumed by ovumcy-web's TestCycleProjection_GoldenVectors; ovumcy-app's existing reference test decodes only `vectors` and ignores this key until its twin consumer lands. See docs/cycle-prediction.md.

vectors.name: median-vs-mean [28,28,28,28,60]: projects from median 28, not mean 34
DST spring-forward (Europe/Berlin 2026-03-29): boundary rollover stays calendar-correct
boundary-day projection: today exactly one cycle out rolls to cycle day 1

irregularRange.$comment: Irregular range mode: the current cycle's fertile window is [PredictCycleWindow(min).fertilityStart, PredictCycleWindow(max).ovulationDate] (irregularFertilityWindow), where `cycleLength` is the median prediction length. A shortest cycle below the 15-day floor (no calculable window) starts the window at lastPeriodStart; the same start clamp applies to a 15-day cycle whose window would begin before it. A longest cycle below the floor leaves the median window's end in place. A window whose last day falls after 9999-12-31 is withheld as a whole (`withheld: true`, null dates). Consumed by ovumcy-web's TestIrregularRangeWindow_GoldenVectors; ovumcy-app has no twin consumer yet and ignores this key. See docs/cycle-prediction.md.

vectors.name: min == max (21): the window is the single cycle's own window
min 15: window start clamped to the cycle start
min 14 (below the 15-day floor): start falls back to the cycle start
min 10 (far below the floor): start falls back to the cycle start
max 14 (below the floor): end falls back to the median window end
9999 edge: window ending exactly on 9999-12-31 is kept
9999 cut: window ending one day past 9999-12-31 is withheld as a whole
